paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when you need Jesus, go to Him and don't hold back. Two blind men heard that He was passing by, and they cried out, "Lord, Son of David, have mercy on us!" (Matthew 20:30). They didn't have much, but they had a need and they knew who could meet it. I think that's where every one of us starts, with an honest cry for mercy.

Now, the crowd told them to be silent, and they cried out all the louder (Matthew 20:31). Friend, some voices around you will say, "Tone it down." Those two did not need a committee vote to keep praying. And look what happens: Jesus stopped and called them (Matthew 20:32). Your cry is NOT a bother to Him.

Then He asks, "What do you want Me to do for you?" (Matthew 20:32). He asks, and they answer plainly: "let our eyes be opened" (Matthew 20:33). Moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and at once they received their sight and followed Him (Matthew 20:34). So tell Him what you need, baker, and when He answers, follow Him. After my years in that drawer, I can tell you the one who answers is worth following.
